analysis.title: Sunday Start | What's Next in Global Macro: 2027 Outlook: Embracing Risk
key_insights: Morgan Stanley takes a broadly positive stance on risk for 2027. It cites an AI capex cycle it views as intact, a resilient global economy, and solid earnings growth extending into 2027. It also notes major risk catalysts are behind us and risk assets have cheapened over the past six months.

Economists expect global growth to soften modestly in 2027 and return to the 2026 pace in 2028 as energy headwinds recede. Growth has modestly exceeded their mid-year expectations, led by US strength and a broadening global investment cycle.

The energy shock has renewed price pressures. Wide spreads between crude and refined products, plus regional differences in delivered prices, mean crude alone is an incomplete inflation gauge. Combined with food and supply-chain pressures, energy costs could feed into core inflation and prompt tighter policy, particularly in emerging markets.

The base case assumes a brief central bank tightening cycle, which depends on energy relief arriving. Persistent inflation that crimps growth is the key risk and sits in the downside scenario. Energy headwinds are expected to recede by end-2027.

The US remains the principal engine of global growth, supported by accelerating AI infrastructure investment and consumer spending backed by wealth and full employment. Europe expands moderately on German fiscal support and periphery growth. China's growth is modest as a deflationary cycle fades. Asia's industrial investment is broadening.
AI capex is critical for US growth and for global growth through exports. Equity analysts kept their baseline investment projections despite policy uncertainty after the US midterm elections.

Elevated funding costs and record borrowing needs call for a quality bias. In US equities, strategists favor strong balance sheets, durable margins and cash generation. The expected shift toward cyclicals remains a rotation within quality.
In credit, Morgan Stanley raises US investment grade to equal weight and cuts high yield to underweight. It also moves up in quality within hard-currency EM sovereigns and securitized credit.

Credit markets should play a larger role in funding AI capex in 2027, bridging the gap between investment and monetization. High-quality issuers keep access to multiple financing channels, while lower-rated participants rely more on asset-backed financing, often supported by higher-rated counterparties.

Portfolio stance: maximum overweight in global equities alongside a neutral allocation to US Treasuries. Duration is kept because equity exposure is high. Uncertainty and tail risks still argue for portfolio protection.
Fewer macro shocks are expected in the base case, with more weight on shifts beneath the surface. Focus is on evidence of returns to AI capex in hyperscaler earnings and broader AI adoption.

US Retail Sales forecast for October (Tue Nov 17): headline flat, retail control +0.2% m/m. Transaction data show softness. Consumption growth is forecast to slow from 3.8% q/q annualized in 3Q to 1.6% in 4Q, with 4Q GDP at 2.2%.

Other US data this week: industrial production forecast -0.4% m/m, housing starts +8.1% m/m (multifamily +19%, single-family +3.6% to 890k), and pending home sales expected to deteriorate further as tighter monetary policy passes through to housing.
UK CPI (Wed Nov 18) forecast at 3.65% y/y headline, 2.77% core and 3.76% services, with the rise driven by auto fuel prices, base effects in transport, and a tobacco duty hike.

Tighter policy where growth is vulnerable, particularly in emerging markets.
Elevated funding costs and record borrowing needs, which favor higher-quality issuers.
Insufficient returns to AI capex, with focus on hyperscaler earnings and broader AI adoption.

tension_points.bull_case: Morgan Stanley's base case is a brief tightening cycle, with energy headwinds receding by end-2027 and global growth returning to its 2026 pace in 2028.
tension_points.bear_case: More persistent inflation from energy, food and supply-chain pressures feeds into core inflation and prompts tighter policy even where growth is vulnerable, crimping growth.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Energy relief failing to materialize, since the brief tightening cycle assumes that relief arrives.
